title: This $42M 'AI' Shopping App Actually Used Hundreds of Humans
alt_title_1: DOJ & SEC: 'Autonomous AI' Checkout App Used Call Centers
alt_title_2: Inside the Federal Indictment of AI Shopping Startup Nate
description_hook: In April 2025, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York and the SEC charged the former CEO of shopping app startup Nate, alleging the company raised over $42 million on claims of autonomous AI checkout while contractors in the Philippines and Romania manually placed orders.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 48-Case Lawsuit & Refund Dossier + Forensics Reading List
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: How many '100% AI' startups today are actually running on manual labor behind the curtain? Full SDNY indictment PDF is in the description.

scenes.headline: Humans Typed Orders Overseas
scenes.narration: Prosecutors charged a 42 million dollar AI shopping startup, alleging overseas workers typed its orders.
scenes.source: U.S. v. Saniger Indictment Count One, p. 1 (S.D.N.Y.)

scenes.headline: Claimed 93% to 97% AI Success
scenes.narration: Investors were allegedly pitched autonomous AI finishing universal checkouts at 93 to 97 percent accuracy.
scenes.source: U.S. v. Albert Saniger Indictment Para. 5, p. 3 (S.D.N.Y.)

scenes.headline: Did Not Use AI to Buy
scenes.narration: The indictment alleges Nate did not use AI to complete purchases, relying instead on manual staff.
scenes.source: U.S. v. Saniger Indictment Para. 7-8, p. 4 (S.D.N.Y.)

scenes.headline: SDNY & SEC Filed Charges
scenes.narration: The Southern District and SEC indicted its former CEO, who remains presumed innocent pending court trial.
scenes.source: U.S. Attorney's Office S.D.N.Y. & SEC LR-26282 (Apr 2025)

scenes.headline: Audit Live Inputs, Not Demos
scenes.narration: Staged startup demos never prove real automation. Always test software live with messy unscripted inputs.
